## {.content background-color="#d6ebe0" .sec1}

<!-- point 1a -->
::: {.cbody}
::: {.incremental}
- Thirst for correctness
- Modular problem solving
- Ability to think deeply
- Raw math skills and knowledge
:::

[Rigour]{.fragment .below-note}
[more or less obvious]{.fragment .below-note}
:::

## {.content background-color="#d6ebe0" .sec1}

<!-- point 1b -->
::: {.cbody}
::: {.incremental}
- Used to being wrong---so okay to change mind
- welcome others who challenge thought process, definitely not offended
    - This is not common.
    - Parents, schoolmates, PhD mates, office mates all get upset
    - B Math folks don't
:::

[Detach self / ego from content of argument]{.fragment .below-note}
:::

## {.content background-color="#d2e6f1" .sec2}

<!-- point 2a: takeaway = "Communication, sales" -->
::: {.cbody}
::: {.incremental}
- How to sell your work
- Correctness $\neq$ precision
    - Omit needless words
    - people (or AI models) forget context
- Tailor what you say based on audience
    - one slide output for leadership $\neq$ detailed proof for a peer
:::
:::

## {.content background-color="#d2e6f1" .sec2}

<!-- point 2b: takeaway = "Decent + quick > Perfect + very slow" -->
::: {.cbody}
::: {.incremental}
- Let perfect not be an enemy of the good
    - When is incorrect good enough?
- Tradeoff of correctness vs speed and delivery
    - bird in hand worth two in bush
    - chicken in hand worth peacock in bush
- How to not be a control freak and trust others
:::

[Decent + quick > Perfect + abysmally slow]{.fragment .below-note}
:::

## {.content background-color="#d2e6f1" .sec2}

<!-- point 2c: takeaway = "Politics: convincing others" -->
::: {.cbody}
::: {.incremental}
- **Politics**
    - different people have different things they care about
    - how to get all of them to align
    - and align in the direction **you** want
:::
:::

## {.content background-color="#f4d8cf" .sec3}

<!-- point 3b (i): mathematical logic; takeaway = "Universality of mathematical logic" -->
::: {.cbody}
::: {.incremental}
- Mathematical logic
    - $p \Longrightarrow q \equiv {\sim} p \lor q$
    - _If **x**, then **y**_
    - _Muggles think: "**x**, hence **y**" or $p \land q$_
:::
:::

## {.content background-color="#f4d8cf" .sec3}

<!-- point 3b (ii): universality -->
::: {.cbody}
::: {.incremental}
- law of excluded middle
    - just because something is not 'right' does not mean it is 'wrong'
- there need not be only one right way
    - एकं सत् विप्रा बहुधा वदन्ति (Rigveda Book 1, Hymn 1.164, Verse 46)
    - _the truth is one, the wise speak it in many ways_
    - does not mean everything is right and nothing is wrong
:::

[mathematical reasoning is not the only valid form of logic or deduction]{.fragment .below-note}
:::

## {.content background-color="#d2e6f1" .sec2}

<!-- inserted: math != science; takeaway = "math != science" -->
[Math $\neq$ science]{.chead}

::: {.cbody}
::: {.incremental}
- In science you have a theory, and collect evidence
    - the first evidence to the contrary: theory is 'wrong'
- In math, you have a theorem, and you prove it
    - there is no doubt about correctness
    - of course, conditional on axioms etc
:::

[all models are wrong, but some are useful]{.fragment .below-note}
:::

[any statement applicable in real life,]{.fragment}
